notices.short_title: Temporary Personnel Services
notices.description:
The Office of Innovation and Technology (OTI), on behalf of the Mayor's Office of Media and Entertainment (MOME or the Agency), is seeking an appropriately qualified vendor (Contractor) to provide temporary personnel services as requested by MOME on an as-needed basis.

This solicitation is released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal, as an RFx. Responses to this solicitation must be submitted via PASSPort.
To reach the Public Portal, visit the following site: https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/passport/about-passport.page then click on the rectangle captioned Procurement Navigator, whereupon you will arrive at the Portal.

Please visit https://passport.cityofnewyork.us/page.aspx/en/rfp/request_browse_public and search by EPIN 85827B0001 to view all information and the documents of this solicitation.

All questions or inquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in the PASSPort Discussion Forum.

notices.short_title: COMPASS School-Based NAQ
notices.description: Pursuant to Section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(A) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) requests approval to enter into a noncompetitive Negotiated Acquisition with the seven (7) providers to provide programming at 11 middle school locations. This procurement maintains critical, uninterrupted Comprehensive After-School System (COMPASS) programming across eleven (11) NYC public schools. These specific school sites were not awarded a contract under the recently concluded competitive solicitation, COMPASS Programs in Public Schools RFP (EPIN: 26026P0003). However, the seven providers selected for this Negotiated Acquisition are the incumbent contractors at these exact schools. They possess proven track records of satisfactory performance, have built deep roots within their respective school communities, and are uniquely positioned to prevent a lapse in critical student services.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Hands in 4 Youth Inc. a $204,750 negotiated contract, without open competition, to continue after-school programming at 11 New York City public middle schools.
